title: Honey-Glazed Pear and Fig Tart
changes_from_base: Baked figs and pears glazed with honey in a blind-baked case, with no crème pâtissière.
summary: Halved figs and fanned pear slices baked in a crisp pastry case and brushed with warm honey.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
small ripe figs, stalks removed, halved
ripe Conference or Bosc pears (about 225 g)

steps.title: Pastry
steps.text: pulse the flour, icing sugar and salt, add the butter and pulse to crumbs, then add the yolk and enough water for the dough to clump. Wrap and chill 30 min.

steps.title: Case
steps.text: roll the dough to 28 cm, line the tin, trim and chill 20 min. Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan).

steps.title: Blind bake
steps.text: line with paper and beans and bake on the tray 20 min, then uncover and bake 5-8 min more, until pale golden.

steps.title: Arrange
steps.text: set the fig halves, cut side up, in a ring round the edge. Quarter, core and peel the pears, cut them across into 8 mm slices and fan them, slightly overlapping, inside the figs. Sprinkle with the sugar. Thin, even slices bake through at the same time as the figs.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: about 35 min, until the fruit is soft and juicy.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: warm the honey gently and brush it over the hot fruit. Serve warm or at room temperature. Brushing the fruit while hot helps the honey soak in.

tips: Pick figs that are soft and fragrant with no splits.
Rub the cut pears with lemon if you prepare them ahead.
A spoon of thick yoghurt or cream is lovely on the side.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day.
